threat_actors.name: Unnamed Espionage Actor
threat_actors.description: A sophisticated, unnamed threat actor with a likely espionage focus that was observed conducting limited, targeted exploitation of a zero-day vulnerability in a major cloud provider's multi-tenant container infrastructure.
threat_actors.goals: To pivot between customer workloads in a multi-tenant cloud environment, likely for espionage purposes.

attack_patterns.name: Escape to Host
attack_patterns.description: The vulnerability allows a malicious actor to break out of their designated container and gain access to the underlying host or, more critically, to the containers of other tenants on the same shared hardware.

attack_patterns.name: Exploitation for Privilege Escalation
attack_patterns.description: The zero-day vulnerability allows an attacker who has already established a foothold within their own containerized workload to escalate privileges, enabling a multi-tenant escape.

attack_patterns.name: Valid Accounts: Cloud Accounts
attack_patterns.description: The vulnerability is linked to weaknesses in identity federation and token-signing for workload identities, allowing an attacker to potentially forge or manipulate an identity token to gain privileges beyond their own tenant's scope, effectively abusing cloud account trust mechanisms.

vulnerabilities.name: Cloud Multi-Tenant Privilege Escalation Zero-Day
vulnerabilities.description: A critical zero-day vulnerability in a major, unnamed cloud provider's multi-tenant containerized infrastructure. The flaw, related to weaknesses in workload identity federation and token-signing processes, allows for privilege escalation and tenant isolation breakout, enabling attackers to pivot between customer workloads.

identities.name: U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA)
identities.description: Issued a bulletin in response to the zero-day vulnerability, advising organizations to validate their cloud security posture, logging, and isolation policies.

identities.name: Unnamed Major Cloud Provider
identities.description: A top-tier cloud service provider (implied to be AWS, Azure, or GCP) affected by the zero-day vulnerability in its multi-tenant containerized environment.

identities.name: Cloud Service Customers
identities.description: Customers of the unnamed cloud provider whose workloads were at risk of tenant isolation breakout due to the zero-day vulnerability.

indicators.name: Anomalous Cross-Account Cloud Role Assumption
indicators.pattern:
title: Anomalous Cross-Account Cloud Role Assumption
id: 2b1f8c8a-4e9d-4f1a-b3c2-1d9e8a7b6c5d
status: experimental
description: Detects anomalous privilege escalation events or cross-account access that is not explicitly authorized, which could indicate a tenant breakout attempt.
references:
  - https://medium.com/@sales_95837/cyber-security-monday-cloud-zero-day-edition-august-3-2026-5d5d8276f2db
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-04
tags:
  - attack.t1068
  - attack.t1078.004
level: high
logsource:
  category: cloud
  service: audit
detection:
  selection:
    event_name: 'AssumeRole'
    # This logic assumes source_identity.account_id and destination_identity.account_id fields exist.
    # The actual fields will vary by cloud provider (e.g., AWS CloudTrail, Azure Monitor).
    source_identity.account_id: 'some_account_id'
    destination_identity.account_id: 'a_different_account_id'
  filter_known_good:
    # Exclude legitimate, documented cross-account roles.
    source_identity.arn|contains:
      - 'arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/KnownCrossAccountRole'
  condition: selection and not filter_known_good
indicators.description: Detects anomalous privilege escalation events or cross-account access that is not explicitly authorized, based on hunting hints for the cloud zero-day.

indicators.name: Suspicious Shell Spawned in Container
indicators.pattern:
title: Suspicious Shell Spawned in Container
id: 9e8d7c6b-5a4b-4c3d-b2a1-f0e9d8c7b6a5
status: experimental
description: Detects the execution of a common shell within a container by a process that is not itself a shell. This can indicate an unexpected interactive session or reverse shell, potentially resulting from a container escape or privilege escalation.
references:
  - https://medium.com/@sales_95837/cyber-security-monday-cloud-zero-day-edition-august-3-2026-5d5d8276f2db
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-04
tags:
  - attack.t1611
  - attack.execution
level: medium
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/sh'
      - '/bash'
      - '/ash'
      - '/zsh'
      - '/csh'
      - '/ksh'
  filter_legit_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '/sh'
      - '/bash'
      - '/ash'
      - '/zsh'
      - '/csh'
      - '/ksh'
      - '/sshd'
      - '/sudo'
      - '/su'
  condition: selection and not filter_legit_parent
indicators.description: Detects unexpected shell processes within a containerized workload, which could indicate a successful privilege escalation or escape.
